relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with Majeed syndrome: 'The panel detected the presence of two novel compound heterozygous mutations in the LPIN2 gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans. No tables in the paper. In scope: the index girl ('patient', rule 5), her mother and father (each stated to carry one of the two variants, so tested relatives; no zygosity or phenotype given for them), and the two Turkish siblings with Majeed syndrome from ref [8] (Discussion), included under the v4 passing-mention rule because a feature (neutropenia) is stated for them; no variant rows for them because no variant is printed. The 'one patient of Puerto Rican and African American descent [2, 7, 8]' / 'case recently described with Puerto Rican and African American descent [7, 8]' was left out: only ancestry is given and the citation names several papers. Variant strings: protein and cDNA printed together ('I716Vfs*2 (c.2144_2145dupGT)', 'p. E565Kfs*15 (c.1693_1694delGA)'); exon 16 and exon 12 stated; no transcript printed. Pathogenicity, ACMG, frameshift class and functional evidence were filled for the patient only, not for the carrier parents (D-29). Normal-finding rows (D-27): 'leucocytes and platelets within the normal range' recorded as abnormal leukocyte/platelet count excluded at 23 months; 'Microbiological investigations were negative' recorded as the paper writes it (excludes nothing more specific). Neutropenia appeared later during anakinra treatment, so the earlier normal leukocyte count was not treated as a contradiction. Checklist judgement calls left 'not reported': CRMO (paper describes multifocal bilateral bone STIR lesions, periosteal reaction and biopsy inflammation but never calls her case CRMO; it only says 'resembling CRMO' in general advice); bone pain (paper says 'pain in the lower limbs', not bone pain); recurrent fever ('low-grade fever' at 6 months and 'no more febrile episodes were reported' after anakinra imply episodes but recurrence is not stated); elevated proinflammatory cytokines (only ex vivo LPS-stimulated monocyte secretion, recorded as a phenotypic feature). Neutrophilic dermatosis excluded from 'no skin involvement was observed' (broader absence). 'As in our patient, neutropenia did not improve after the beginning of treatment with anakinra' may refer to the ref [8] siblings; ambiguous, so no treatment recorded for them. No contradictions found in the paper.
